events.title: Columbus's Expedition Nears Land
events.description: On the night of October 11-12, 1492, Christopher Columbus's crew sighted signs of land, including floating vegetation and branches, shortly before Rodrigo de Triana spotted land in the early hours of October 12 in the Bahamas.
events.significance: This voyage opened sustained contact between Europe and the Americas, with profound consequences for global trade, colonization, and the peoples of both hemispheres.

events.title: Launch of the Steam-Powered Ferry Juliana
events.description: Inventor John Stevens launched the Juliana, the first steam-powered ferry, which began operating between New York City and Hoboken, New Jersey.
events.significance: The Juliana was an early milestone in commercial steamboat service and helped demonstrate the viability of steam-powered passenger transport.

events.title: Opening of the Second Vatican Council
events.description: Pope John XXIII formally opened the Second Vatican Council in St. Peter's Basilica, gathering thousands of bishops from around the world.
events.significance: The Council modernized many Catholic practices, including allowing Mass in vernacular languages and promoting ecumenical dialogue, reshaping the Church in the modern era.

events.title: Launch of Apollo 7
events.description: NASA launched Apollo 7, the first crewed mission of the Apollo program, carrying Wally Schirra, Donn Eisele, and Walter Cunningham on an 11-day Earth-orbit flight.
events.significance: The mission successfully tested the Apollo command and service module and included the first live TV broadcasts from American spacecraft, paving the way for the Apollo 8 lunar orbit mission and the Moon landings.

events.title: Birth of Eleanor Roosevelt
events.description: Anna Eleanor Roosevelt was born in New York City. She became First Lady of the United States during Franklin D. Roosevelt's presidency and later a diplomat and activist.
events.significance: She chaired the UN commission that drafted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and redefined the role of First Lady as an advocate for civil rights and social reform.
